title: 《高等微積分》第 86 集｜置換與正負號｜Loomis & Sternberg 第 7 章 §3–§4
description:
本集是 Loomis 與 Sternberg《Advanced Calculus》第 7 章第 3 節「置換」與第 4 節「置換的正負號」（書頁 308 到 310）。第 7 章整章沒有習題。

這一段是純組合的，但它撐起整章：交錯是用置換的正負號定義的，而行列式就是唯一的交錯 m 重形式。

置換在複合之下封閉、有反元素、有單位元、結合律成立，那就是一個群。最簡單的非單位置換是交換兩個元素，叫做對換，而任何置換都能寫成對換的乘積——分解法不唯一，但**長度的奇偶不變**。畫面把四個元素的二十四個置換全部分解、再乘回去逐一比對，並用廣度優先搜尋找出長度五以內的所有分解，驗每個置換的所有分解長度模二相同。

接著是置換怎麼作用在泛函上。定義寫成 f 作用後在 ξ 上的值等於 f 在 ξ 複合 σ 的反元素上的值——**為什麼用反元素**是這一節的關鍵，因為只有這樣才會有引理 3.1 那個複合關係。畫面把不用反元素的版本也算了：三十六組裡有十八組不成立，而且它滿足的是順序寫反的那一條。

定理 3.1 說每個置換給出一個線性同構，而那個對應是**反同態**——複合的順序會顛倒過來。這一點畫面上同樣用數字分出對錯：對的那個順序三十六組全中，反過來的那個有十八組不成立。引理 3.2 說每個這樣的算子只是把基底重新排列，畫面上八個多重指標排在同一個圈上，六支箭頭是兩條三角路徑、兩個圈起來的留在原地。

最後是正負號。書上用一個特別的多項式，它是所有 i 小於 j 的差的乘積；置換作用在它上面只會改變某些因式的符號，而負一的那個次方就叫 sgn。畫面把四個元素的二十四個置換全部驗過，並且驗 sgn 的乘法性與「對換的 sgn 是負一」。有了 sgn 就能定義交錯，那是下一集的事。

title: Advanced Calculus, Episode 86 | Permutations and the Sign | Ch. 7, §3-4
description:
This episode is sections 3 and 4 of chapter 7 of Loomis and Sternberg's Advanced Calculus, permutations and the sign of a permutation, pages 308 to 310. Chapter 7 has no exercises.

This stretch is pure combinatorics, and it carries the chapter: alternating is defined through the sign of a permutation, and the determinant is the unique alternating m-linear form.

Permutations are closed under composition, have inverses and an identity, and compose associatively, which is exactly a group. The simplest non-identity permutation swaps two elements, and every permutation is a product of such swaps -- not uniquely, but the parity of the length never changes. On screen all twenty-four permutations of four elements are factored and multiplied back together one by one, and a breadth-first search finds every factorisation of length five or less, confirming that all factorisations of a given permutation have the same length modulo two.

Then comes the action on functionals, defined so that the acted-on functional at a point equals the original at the point composed with the inverse. Why the inverse is the point of the section: only that convention gives Lemma 3.1 its composition law. The version without the inverse is computed as well, and it fails on eighteen of thirty-six pairs, while satisfying the law with the order reversed.

Theorem 3.1 makes each permutation a linear isomorphism, and the correspondence an antihomomorphism: composition comes out in the opposite order. The screen separates right from wrong numerically here too, with the correct order holding on all thirty-six pairs and the reverse failing on eighteen. Lemma 3.2 says each such operator merely rearranges the basis, and the figure puts all eight multi-indices on one circle, where the six arrows form two triangular paths while the two ringed ones stay where they are.

Last is the sign. The book uses a particular polynomial, the product of all the differences for i less than j; a permutation acting on it only changes the signs of some factors, and minus one to that power is the sign. All twenty-four permutations of four elements are verified, along with the multiplicativity of the sign and the fact that a transposition has sign minus one. With the sign in hand, alternating can be defined, which is the next episode.
